items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he taught me how to read drum music. He taught me, you know, about the notes, note value, quarter notes, eighth note, sixteenth notes

ctx.x: Yeah, Billy Exner, who went on to play with Tony Bennett. I guess that was his biggest claim to fame but he obviously was a man of big heart to share his talent in time with you.

Yeah, first of all man, he was a dynamite dude. I mean I can’t say enough accolades, good things about him. But as well as being a fantastic musician, he was fantastic drummer man and he could swing. And at that time man, the most important thing is -- you know, like from the beginning, if you could swing, if you had a beat, you had that pulse, you get that pulse going, that’s all you had to do, you know. And you’d work all the time, you know. And Billy was fantastic man, plus the fact man, taking the time to…
He taught me, you know, about the notes, note value, quarter notes, eighth note, sixteenth notes and he showed me what they looked like and from then on man it’s dynamite.
